Check tables against a specification: structure, types, missing-value codes, value domains and keys

Source: R/check_conformance.R
gpq_check_conformance.Rd

Runs the conformance stage on a set of related tables: pre-flight of the specification and configuration, then the checks of the layers asked for, each table and column read as the specification describes it. Returns the results summary and one issue per failing record, or one per column where a rule fails on every record of a column in a group.

Usage

gpq_check_conformance(
  tables,
  spec,
  table_map = NULL,
  group_cols = NULL,
  problem_unit = NULL,
  rules = NULL,
  layers = 0:5,
  settings = list(),
  run_id = NULL
)

Arguments

tables

The tables, one per table of the specification, named as it names them: a named list whose elements are data.frames or paths of CSV files, mixed as you like, or a named character vector of paths. Every column of a CSV file is read as text, so class_mismatch and integer_stored_as_double don't run on its tables. In a CSV file an empty cell is a missing value and everything else is read as written, so write files with data.table::fwrite(). A cell that isn't valid UTF-8 is read as Windows-1252, unless it holds a byte Windows-1252 doesn't define. A table holding text marked as bytes is refused. Or a DBI connection: the specification's tables are read from it under the names table_map gives, and its other tables are left alone. A column stored as integer64 needs the bit64 package: the run loads it, and stops if it isn't installed.

spec

A specification from gpq_read_spec() or magp_spec().

table_map

NULL, or, when tables is a DBI connection, a named character vector of the database's names for tables of the specification: names the specification's table names, values the database's, such as c(trees = "survey.tree_list") for the table tree_list in the schema survey. A table it doesn't name is read under its own name. A table of the specification the database doesn't have is reported as missing (table_missing).

group_cols

NULL, or the grouping columns, report unit first: results and issues carry them under these names.

problem_unit

NULL, or list(table, key_col): the table and key column of the unit problem plots are ranked by; issues carry that key under its name.

rules

NULL, or a rule set such as magp_rules() returns.

layers

The layers to run, whole numbers from 0 to 5.

settings

A named list of settings.

run_id

NULL, to make one from the run's start, or a run ID such as "20261215T140312Z_3fa9c1": the UTC start time and six hex characters.

Value

An object of class gpq_results, a list of three tables and the run metadata:

  • results: the summary, one row per rule, table, column and group: run_id, run_scope, rule_id, rule_fingerprint, stage, layer, severity, table_name, column_name, the group columns, n_checked, n_fail, n_not_evaluated, reason_code, n_distinct_fail_values, n_easy_fix, examples, status (pass, fail or not_run), not_run_reason and message_id.

  • issues: one row per failing or not-evaluated record, or per column-level issue: issue_id, run_id, run_scope, rule_id, rule_fingerprint, stage, layer, severity, reason_code, table_name, column_name, record_pk, row_number, pk_positional, level (record or column), n_records, value, expected, entity_key, visit_keys, provider_key, provider_key_status, the group columns, the problem unit's key column, root_issue_id, status (open or not_evaluated), issue_class, class_basis, script_file, script_block, attribution_status, fingerprint, fingerprint_pk, first_seen_run, change and change_cause. The columns a conformance run doesn't fill are NA.

  • corrections: an empty table.

  • metadata: the tables of metadata/ in a run folder.

Write it with gpq_write_results().

Details

Pre-flight (gpq_preflight()) runs before any check, on spec, rules and settings; it stops the run where it would stop, and its warning reaches the caller. The checks never change tables.

A CSV file is read with data.table::fread(), which finds its separator. A file it can't read cleanly, such as one with a ragged line or a title line shorter than its header, stops the run before any check, and so does a file that doesn't end with a line break, which may be cut off. A title line as long as the header, or above a file of one column, is read as the header, so the checks report the file's columns as missing. The run's inputs metadata names each file with its SHA-256, its rows, its separator and how many values were read as Windows-1252. A table read from a DBI connection is recorded as "DBI connection, not hashed", with the database's name for it and the driver's class.

Layers and the rules they can raise:

  • Layer 0, structure: table_missing, table_unexpected, column_missing, column_unexpected, column_name_mismatch.

  • Layer 1, data types: class_mismatch, coercion_loss, date_unparseable, integer_stored_as_double, value_not_finite.

  • Layer 2, missing-value codes: raw_na, blank_string, sentinel_wrong_type, sentinel_rogue_code, species_unknown_code, whitespace_padding, na_text_in_id.

  • Layer 3, value domains: code_not_in_list, value_below_min, value_above_max, string_too_long, pattern_mismatch, decimals_exceeded, site_id_out_of_range, coordinate_out_of_bounds, undeclared_code_set.

  • Layer 4, keys and relationships: pk_duplicate, pk_missing, fk_orphan, fk_unassigned, fk_sentinel_unverified, fk_not_applicable_mismatch, src_id_duplicate, key_incoherent, record_unreachable, parent_without_children, design_geometry_inconsistent, subplot_label_ambiguous, design_duplicate_signature.

Two of these write no issue at this version: parent_without_children counts, in the results only, the parent records that no child record names, and fk_not_applicable_mismatch writes only not_run rows until a version brings the applicability matrix. record_unreachable runs only when gpq_read_spec() was given reach, and the design checks only when their settings name their tables and columns; otherwise each writes one not_run row (no_input).

Layer 5 has no rules yet. A column whose name differs from its dictionary attribute's only in letter case or spaces is reported by column_name_mismatch and checked as that attribute. class_mismatch, integer_stored_as_double, undeclared_code_set and Layer 0's rules count tables or columns, not records, and their rows have "*" in every group column. A value that failed Layer 1 is not evaluated by Layer 2: its issue there has status not_evaluated and names the earlier issue as its root. A value that failed Layer 1 or 2 is not evaluated by Layer 3's record rules, which leave a missing value, a blank, a missing-value code and an unknown code to Layer 2. A value that failed Layer 1 or 2 is not evaluated by Layer 4. Nor is one that failed Layer 3, unless it is in a primary or foreign key column: such a value still joins, so Layer 4 checks it as a key. Masking applies only to a record's own values: key_incoherent and the design checks still use values they read from other records, even ones that failed an earlier layer in those records. Layer 4 leaves a key that is missing, blank or a missing-value code the key can't hold to pk_missing and fk_unassigned, counts a foreign key's missing-value code that it may hold as not evaluated in fk_orphan (and warns of it in fk_sentinel_unverified where the key is a number), and doesn't evaluate record_unreachable on a record pk_missing reports. When a rule fails on every checked record of a column in a group, and at least column_level_min_n records were checked, the run records one column-level issue; masked records sharing one root collapse the same way.

A record's group values are read from its own table, or from the nearest table that holds the column, through the foreign keys; a record that can't reach one, whose keys on the way don't match, or whose value there is blank or missing, has "*" there. A group value marked latin1 is converted to UTF-8 and runs; one whose bytes aren't valid UTF-8 stops the run, naming the column, the table it is read from and its first such row.

Settings (each from the argument, the rule set, the option, or the built-in value, see groundplotqc_options): raw_na_policy, rogue_codes, unknown_codes, coordinate_attributes, code_set_max_values, code_set_skip_attributes, code_set_skip_pattern, design_geometry_table, design_geometry_by, design_geometry_columns, subplot_label_table, subplot_label_columns, design_signature_table, design_signature_by, design_signature_columns, column_level_min_n, example_cap, lang and severity. A rule set's rules rows give a rule's severity and turn it off (enabled) for a table and attribute: the most specific row that gives a value wins (table and attribute, then table and "*", then "*" and attribute, then "*" and "*"). A rule turned off writes no rows there.

See also

gpq_preflight(), which the run calls first; gpq_decode_lineage() and gpq_classify_issues(), which give its issues their provider keys and classes.

Examples

# magp_example with one planted defect: a missing value in a column that must hold one.
trees <- data.table::copy(magp_example$magp_trees)
trees$tree_dist[1] <- NA
planted <- magp_example
planted$magp_trees <- trees
# MAGPlot's bundled specification has known pre-flight warnings, so this warning is expected.
results <- gpq_check_conformance(
  planted, magp_spec(),
  group_cols = c("magp_contributor_id", "jurisdiction", "magp_dataset_id"),
  problem_unit = list("magp_plots", "magp_plot_id"), rules = magp_rules(), layers = 0:2
)
#> Warning: Pre-flight found 32 warning(s); see the returned table.
table(results$results$status)
#> 
#> fail pass 
#>    1 7930 
results$issues[results$issues$status == "open", c("rule_id", "table_name", "column_name")]
#>    rule_id table_name column_name
#>     <char>     <char>      <char>
#> 1:  raw_na magp_trees   tree_dist
